claim.why_it_matters: Plain paragraph rather than a heading; the outline loses clause IV.4.2, the parent of the '### 4.2.2 Character-Strings' heading on page 151.

verdict.reasoning: The rendered page (folio IV-4) prints '4.2  LANGUAGE STRUCTURE' as a numbered section heading on its own line, set like '4.1 CHARACTER SET' and '4.2.1 Separators'. The markdown page-150.md holds the text word for word, but as a plain paragraph line with no '#' markup. Line 6391 of specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md marks its child '4.2.2 Character-Strings' as '### 4.2.2 Character-Strings', and grep shows that 4.1, 4.2 and 4.2.1 carry no heading markup. So the outline really does lose clause IV.4.2, and the child 4.2.2 sits under the wrong parent. The wording is unchanged, so normative content is unaffected. The problem is structural only, as the claim's severity says. The claim quotes both sources accurately.
